pages.text: The Ultimate Time Wand creates a time-limited, server-owned acceleration request for one target. By default, it stores $(bold)800,000 mB of Time Fluid$() and $(bold)10,000,000 FE$(). The capacities, duration, and cost multipliers are configurable by the server.$(br2)$(bold)Modes and stacking$()$(br2)Sneak-right-click air or a block to cycle through four modes:$(br2)$(bold)Mode | Exponent added per use$()$(br)Normal | 1$(br)2x | 2$(br)4x | 4$(br)Max | 10$(br2)Normal right-click on a valid target creates a request; right-clicking a target with an existing request adds its exponent. The effect is capped at $(bold)1024x$(), and reaching the cap does not consume resources. The wand accelerates JDT-approved tickable blocks and directly accelerates AE2 devices that expose the $(thing)IGridTickable$() service.

$(bold)Resources and server safety$()$(br2)For each stack, the server validates the target and calculates resource costs before it writes the new request state. Insufficient Time Fluid or FE, an invalid target, a target already at the maximum multiplier, or a failed server commit never consumes resources.$(br2)Requests execute only on the server and are bounded by the per-target batch limit. AE2 targets take the direct acceleration route and never also receive an ordinary block-entity or random-tick execution from the same request. Time accelerators themselves are excluded as targets to prevent recursive acceleration.$(br2)$(bold)Crafting$()
